docs.title: AI Codebase Knowledge Builder
docs.text: Ever stared at a new codebase written by others feeling completely lost? This project analyzes GitHub repositories and creates beginner-friendly tutorials explaining exactly how the code works - all powered by AI! Our intelligent system automatically breaks down complex codebases into digestible explanations that even beginners can understand.

docs.title: 🚀 Getting Started
docs.text:
1. Clone this repository 

    git clone https://github.com/ardennguyen/Codebase-Knowledge-Builder

  2. Install dependencies (we highly recommend using a virtual environment of your choice like venv, conda, uv, or pyenv to avoid polluting your global system): 

    pip install -r requirements.txt

  3. Set up LLM in utils/call_llm.py by providing credentials via a .env file. You can use native Gemini by setting GEMINI_API_KEY. For OpenRouter, set LLM_PROVIDER=OPENROUTER and OPENROUTER_API_KEY.

  4. Generate a complete codebase tutorial by running the main script: 

    # Analyze a GitHub repository
python main.py --repo https://github.com/username/repo --include "*.py" "*.js" --exclude "tests/*" --max-size 50000

# Or, analyze a local directory
python main.py --dir /path/to/your/codebase --include "*.py" --exclude "*test*"

# Or, generate a tutorial in Vietnamese
python main.py --repo https://github.com/username/repo --language "Vietnamese"

docs.title: CLI Options
docs.text:
• --repo or --dir - Specify either a GitHub repo URL or a local directory path (required, mutually exclusive)
  • -n, --name - Project name (optional, derived from URL/directory if omitted)
  • -t, --token - GitHub token (or set GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable)
  • -o, --output - Output directory (default: ./output)
  • -i, --include - Files to include (e.g., *.py *.js). Defaults to * (all files).
  • -e, --exclude - Files to exclude. Custom patterns are automatically merged with a massive global exclusion list (build caches, node_modules, binaries, media, AI environments) AND your repository's native .gitignore rules.
  • -s, --max-size - Maximum file size in bytes (default: 200KB)
  • --language - Language for the generated tutorial (default: "english")
  • --max-abstractions - Maximum number of abstractions to identify (default: 10)
  • --no-cache - Disable LLM response caching (default: caching enabled)
  • --thinking-level - Thinking effort level for native Gemini, OpenRouter, and Ollama reasoning models (e.g., low, medium, high). Leave empty to use model defaults.
  • --max-tokens - Maximum number of tokens for the context window (default: fetched dynamically from the model).
  • --mode - Documentation style (tutorial, advanced, api-reference, sdk). (default: tutorial)
  • --advanced - Legacy flag: equivalent to --mode advanced
  • --mkdocs - Format output for MkDocs Material (adds YAML frontmatter & nav snippet)
  • --incremental - Enable MD5 incremental caching to skip unchanged modules (Only supported in --mode api-reference)
  • --force-rebuild - Clear incremental cache and regenerate all chapters from scratch (use with --incremental)
  • --batch - Maximum files per batch when using map-reduce mode (default: 50).
  • --force-batch - Force the pipeline to use map-reduce mode regardless of context limits.
  • --debug - Enable verbose debug output.
  • --cleanup - Clean up logs and cache JSON at the end of the script (default: No).

The application will crawl the repository, analyze the codebase structure, generate tutorial content in the specified language, and save the output in the specified directory (default: ./output). This includes individual chapter files, an index.md, and a compiled full_content.md containing the complete tutorial with a Table of Contents.

Built using Pocket Flow, a 100-line LLM framework.

docs.title: 1. Requirements
docs.text:
Notes for AI: Keep it simple and clear. If the requirements are abstract, write concrete user stories

User Story: As a developer onboarding to a new codebase, I want a tutorial automatically generated from its GitHub repository or local directory, optionally in a specific language. The system supports four documentation styles: a tutorial mode that explains core abstractions with beginner-friendly language, analogies, and code walkthroughs; an advanced mode that produces architecture deep-dives aimed at senior developers or PMs joining a project mid-way, covering design patterns, key dependencies, and practical onboarding notes; an api-reference mode that generates exhaustive, formal API documentation for every code module (1:1 file-to-chapter mapping); and an sdk mode that produces SDK-style integration guides. The system must also gracefully handle codebases of any size by dynamically switching to a Map-Reduce approach when context limits are reached.

Input: - A publicly accessible GitHub repository URL or a local directory path. - A project name (optional, will be derived from the URL/directory if not provided). - Desired language for the tutorial (optional, defaults to English). - Advanced configurations: documentation style (--mode), token scaling (--max-tokens, --batch, --force-batch), prompting (--thinking-level, --max-abstractions), caching (--no-cache), output format (--mkdocs, --incremental), debugging (--debug), and execution cleanup (--cleanup).

Output: - A directory named after the project containing: - An index.md file with: - A high-level project summary (potentially translated). - A Mermaid flowchart diagram visualizing relationships between abstractions (using potentially translated names/labels). - An ordered list of links to chapter files (using potentially translated names). - A link to full_content.md at the bottom. - Individual Markdown files for each chapter (01_chapter_one.md, 02_chapter_two.md, etc.) detailing core abstractions in a logical order (potentially translated content). - A full_content.md (inside the project subdirectory) containing all merged chapters and a Table of Contents. - When --mkdocs is used: YAML frontmatter is injected into every chapter, filenames mirror source directory structure instead of numbered prefixes, and a nav_snippet.yml navigation file is generated for MkDocs integration. - When --incremental is used (api-reference mode only): a .doc_cache_manifest.json tracks MD5 hashes of source files to skip regeneration of unchanged modules across runs.

docs.title: 2. Flow Design
docs.text: Notes for AI: 1. Consider the design patterns of agent, map-reduce, rag, and workflow. Apply them if they fit. 2. Present a concise, high-level description of the workflow.

docs.title: Applicable Design Pattern:
docs.text:
This project primarily uses a Workflow pattern with dynamic branching into a Map-Reduce pattern. The chapter writing step also utilizes a BatchNode.

  1. Workflow & Routing: The overall process fetches code, estimates token payloads, and routes based on context limits. If the codebase fits the LLM window, it goes directly to abstraction identification.
  2. Map-Reduce: If the codebase exceeds context limits (or if forced), the codebase is grouped into token-aware, directory-isolated batches (each batch stays under the effective token limit and never mixes files from different directories). A MapAbstractions BatchNode processes each batch individually, and a ReduceAbstractions Node merges them into a global list.
  3. Batch Processing: The WriteChapters node processes each identified abstraction independently (map) before final tutorial compilation.

docs.title: Flow high-level Design:
docs.text:
1. FetchRepo: Crawls the specified repository/directory using crawl_github_files or crawl_local_files.
  2. ContextRouter: Analyzes the total token payload of the fetched files using tiktoken. Dynamically calculates prompt overhead (template tokens + directory tree tokens) and computes an effective limit = safety_limit - prompt_overhead. If --mode api-reference is used, routes to "deterministic". If the file content tokens exceed this effective limit or if --force-batch is used, it chunks files into token-aware, directory-isolated batches (never mixing files from different directories) and routes to "batch". Also builds a compact directory tree of all files (stored in shared["directory_tree"]) for cross-batch awareness. With --debug, displays detailed per-batch file lists and token breakdowns. Otherwise, it routes to "direct".
  3. Path A: Direct
    • IdentifyAbstractions: Analyzes the entire codebase at once to identify core abstractions.
  4. Path B: Map-Reduce
    • MapAbstractions (BatchNode): Analyzes each localized directory chunk to extract partial abstractions. Each batch receives the full directory tree for cross-batch awareness.
    • ReduceAbstractions: Merges overlapping/partial abstractions into a global list of architecture components.
  5. Path C: Deterministic (api-reference mode)
    • DeterministicFileMapper: Bypasses LLM-based abstraction discovery entirely. Uses a lightweight LLM call to filter out non-code files (configs, UI layouts, static assets), then creates a 1:1 mapping of each code file to a documentation module. Skips AnalyzeRelationships and OrderChapters, routing directly to WriteChapters.
  6. AnalyzeRelationships (Paths A & B only): Takes the unified abstractions list (from either path) and generates a high-level project summary and relationships diagram. Uses token-budget-aware file inclusion: the budget is split evenly across abstractions, with unused budget redistributed in a second pass, maximizing code context without exceeding the context window.
  7. OrderChapters (Paths A & B only): Determines the most logical sequence to present the abstractions.
  8. WriteChapters (BatchNode): Iterates through the ordered abstractions and writes detailed Markdown chapters using context-aware code inclusion.
  9. CombineTutorial: Assembles the final outputs including index.md, individual chapter files, and a compiled full_content.md.
flowchart TD
    A[FetchRepo] --> Router[ContextRouter]

    Router -->|direct| B[IdentifyAbstractions]
    Router -->|batch| M1[MapAbstractions]
    Router -->|deterministic| DFM[DeterministicFileMapper]
    M1 --> M2[ReduceAbstractions]

    B --> C[AnalyzeRelationships]
    M2 --> C

    C --> D[OrderChapters]
    D --> E[Batch WriteChapters]
    DFM --> E
    E --> F[CombineTutorial]

def crawl_local_files(directory, include_patterns=None, exclude_patterns=None,
                      max_file_size=None, use_relative_paths=True) -> dict:
    # Returns: {"files": {relative_path_str: content_str, ...}}

Directory Pruning Algorithm (critical for nested directories like Core.User/.vs/): 

# During os.walk, for each subdirectory d:
excluded_dirs = set()
for d in dirs:
    dirpath_rel = os.path.relpath(os.path.join(root, d), directory)
    # Check .gitignore first
    if gitignore_spec and gitignore_spec.match_file(dirpath_rel):
        excluded_dirs.add(d)
        continue
    # Check exclude patterns — strip trailing /* for directory matching
    if exclude_patterns:
        for pattern in exclude_patterns:
            dir_pattern = pattern[:-2] if pattern.endswith("/*") else pattern
            if fnmatch.fnmatch(dirpath_rel, dir_pattern) or fnmatch.fnmatch(d, dir_pattern):
                excluded_dirs.add(d)
                break
# Remove matched dirs to prevent os.walk descent
for d in dirs.copy():
    if d in excluded_dirs:
        dirs.remove(d)

Note: Directory validation: raises ValueError if directory path doesn't exist. Loads .gitignore with utf-8-sig encoding (BOM-safe). All directories and files are sorted() for deterministic traversal order.

Progress Display Format: - Green (\033[92m): [processed] — Successfully read files - Gray (\033[90m): [excluded (.gitignore)] / [excluded (not in include list)] — Skipped by pattern - Red (\033[91m): [size limit: {size_kb:.0f}KB] — Exceeded max_file_size - Red (\033[91m): [cannot process: not a text file] / [cannot process: {e}] — Binary/encoding errors

Note: After crawling, prints a --- Crawl Summary --- block with total found, processed, excluded, size limited, and non-text counts.

Triggered when repo_url.startswith("git@") or repo_url.endswith(".git"): 

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdirname:
    print(f"Cloning SSH repo {repo_url} to temp dir {tmpdirname} ...")
    try:
        repo = git.Repo.clone_from(repo_url, tmpdirname)
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error cloning repo: {e}")
        return {"files": {}, "stats": {"error": str(e)}}

    files = {}
    skipped_files = []

    # --- ANSI colors ---
    C_GREEN  = "\033[92m"
    C_GRAY   = "\033[90m"
    C_RED    = "\033[91m"
    C_RESET  = "\033[0m"

    # --- Counters ---
    count_processed = 0
    count_excluded = 0
    count_size_limit = 0
    count_non_text = 0
    skipped_size_list = []
    skipped_non_text_list = []
    entry_num = 0

    # --- Load .gitignore (BOM-safe) ---
    gitignore_path = os.path.join(tmpdirname, ".gitignore")
    gitignore_spec = None
    if os.path.exists(gitignore_path):
        try:
            with open(gitignore_path, "r", encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
                gitignore_spec = pathspec.PathSpec.from_lines("gitwildmatch", f.readlines())
        except Exception:
            pass

    for root, dirs, filenames in os.walk(tmpdirname):
        # --- Directory pruning (same algorithm as crawl_local_files) ---
        excluded_dirs = set()
        for d in sorted(dirs):
            dirpath_rel = os.path.relpath(os.path.join(root, d), tmpdirname)
            reason = None
            if gitignore_spec and gitignore_spec.match_file(dirpath_rel):
                reason = "excluded (.gitignore)"
            elif exclude_patterns:
                for pattern in exclude_patterns:
                    dir_pattern = pattern[:-2] if pattern.endswith("/*") else pattern
                    if fnmatch.fnmatch(dirpath_rel, dir_pattern) or fnmatch.fnmatch(d, dir_pattern):
                        reason = "excluded"
                        break
            if reason:
                excluded_dirs.add(d)
                entry_num += 1
                count_excluded += 1
                print(f"{C_GRAY}  [{entry_num}] {dirpath_rel}/ [{reason}]{C_RESET}")

        for d in dirs.copy():
            if d in excluded_dirs:
                dirs.remove(d)
        dirs.sort()  # Deterministic traversal order

        # --- File processing ---
        for filename in sorted(filenames):
            abs_path = os.path.join(root, filename)
            rel_path = os.path.relpath(abs_path, tmpdirname)
            entry_num += 1

            if not should_include_file(rel_path, filename, gitignore_spec=gitignore_spec):
                count_excluded += 1
                print(f"{C_GRAY}  [{entry_num}] {rel_path} [excluded]{C_RESET}")
                continue

            try:
                file_size = os.path.getsize(abs_path)
            except OSError:
                continue

            if file_size > max_file_size:
                count_size_limit += 1
                skipped_size_list.append(rel_path)
                size_kb = file_size / 1024
                print(f"{C_RED}  [{entry_num}] {rel_path} [size limit: {size_kb:.0f}KB]{C_RESET}")
                continue

            try:
                with open(abs_path, "r", encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
                    content = f.read()
                files[rel_path] = content
                count_processed += 1
                print(f"{C_GREEN}  [{entry_num}] {rel_path} [processed]{C_RESET}")
            except (UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError):
                count_non_text += 1
                skipped_non_text_list.append(rel_path)
                print(f"{C_RED}  [{entry_num}] {rel_path} [cannot process: not a text file]{C_RESET}")
            except Exception as e:
                count_non_text += 1
                skipped_non_text_list.append(rel_path)
                print(f"{C_RED}  [{entry_num}] {rel_path} [cannot process: {e}]{C_RESET}")

    # --- Crawl Summary ---
    total_fetched = count_processed + count_excluded + count_size_limit + count_non_text
    print(f"\n--- Crawl Summary ---")
    print(f"  Total found : {total_fetched}")
    print(f"{C_GREEN}  Processed   : {count_processed}{C_RESET}")
    if count_excluded > 0:
        print(f"{C_GRAY}  Excluded    : {count_excluded}{C_RESET}")
    if count_size_limit > 0:
        print(f"{C_RED}  Size limit  : {count_size_limit}{C_RESET}")
        for sf in skipped_size_list:
            print(f"{C_RED}    - {sf}{C_RESET}")
    if count_non_text > 0:
        print(f"{C_RED}  Non-text    : {count_non_text}{C_RESET}")
        for sf in skipped_non_text_list:
            print(f"{C_RED}    - {sf}{C_RESET}")
    print(f"---------------------")

    return {
        "files": files,
        "stats": {
            "downloaded_count": len(files),
            "skipped_count": len(skipped_files),
            "skipped_files": skipped_files,
            "base_path": None,
            "include_patterns": include_patterns,
            "exclude_patterns": exclude_patterns,
            "source": "ssh_clone"
        }
    }

parsed_url = urlparse(repo_url)
path_parts = parsed_url.path.strip('/').split('/')
owner, repo = path_parts[0], path_parts[1]

headers = {"Accept": "application/vnd.github.v3+json"}

Step 2 — Dynamic Branch Detection (handles multi-segment branch names like feature/foo): 

if len(path_parts) > 2 and 'tree' == path_parts[2]:
    join_parts = lambda i: '/'.join(path_parts[i:])

    # Fetch all branches
    branches = fetch_branches(owner, repo)  # GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches
    branch_names = map(lambda b: b.get("name"), branches)

    # Match URL path against branch names (handles multi-segment names)
    relevant_path = join_parts(3)
    ref = next((name for name in branch_names if relevant_path.startswith(name)), None)

    # Fallback: check if it's a commit/tree hash
    if ref is None:
        tree = path_parts[3]
        ref = tree if check_tree(owner, repo, tree) else None  # GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/trees/{tree}

    # Extract subdirectory (accounts for multi-slash branch names)
    part_index = 5 if '/' in ref else 4
    specific_path = join_parts(part_index) if part_index < len(path_parts) else ""
else:
    ref = None  # Let GitHub use default branch
    specific_path = ""

Step 3 — Remote .gitignore Fetch: 

gi_url = f"https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/.gitignore"
gi_params = {"ref": ref} if ref is not None else {}
gi_resp = requests.get(gi_url, headers=headers, params=gi_params, timeout=(10, 10))
if gi_resp.status_code == 200:
    gi_data = gi_resp.json()
    if "content" in gi_data and gi_data.get("encoding") == "base64":
        gi_content = base64.b64decode(gi_data["content"]).decode('utf-8')
        gitignore_spec = pathspec.PathSpec.from_lines("gitwildmatch", gi_content.splitlines())

Step 4 — Recursive Content Fetching (1 API call per directory): 

def fetch_contents(path):
    url = f"https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/{path}"
    params = {"ref": ref} if ref is not None else {}
    response = requests.get(url, headers=headers, params=params, timeout=(30, 30))

    # Rate limit handling with header-based wait:
    if response.status_code in (403, 429) and 'rate limit exceeded' in response.text.lower():
        if not token:
            raise Exception("GitHub API rate limit exceeded. Provide a token.")
        reset_time = int(response.headers.get('X-RateLimit-Reset', 0))
        wait_time = max(reset_time - time.time(), 0) + 1
        time.sleep(wait_time)
        return fetch_contents(path)  # Recursive retry

    contents = response.json()
    if not isinstance(contents, list):
        contents = [contents]

    for item in contents:
        if item["type"] == "file":
            # Check patterns, size, then fetch content
            # Path A: Use download_url directly, check Content-Length header
            # Path B (fallback): If no download_url, GET item["url"],
            #   base64 decode with size estimate: len(content) * 0.75 > max_file_size
        elif item["type"] == "dir":
            # Check gitignore + exclude before recursing
            fetch_contents(item["path"])

Step 5 — Dual Content Fetch Strategy: 

# Path A: download_url available
if "download_url" in item and item["download_url"]:
    file_response = requests.get(item["download_url"], headers=headers, timeout=(30, 30))
    content_length = int(file_response.headers.get('content-length', 0))
    if content_length > max_file_size:  # Final size check
        continue
    files[rel_path] = file_response.text

# Path B: base64 fallback
else:
    content_response = requests.get(item["url"], headers=headers, timeout=(30, 30))
    content_data = content_response.json()
    if len(content_data["content"]) * 0.75 > max_file_size:  # Approximate size
        continue
    file_content = base64.b64decode(content_data["content"]).decode('utf-8')
    files[rel_path] = file_content

Provide a GitHub token." | | 404 | Token, no path, ref='main' | "Repository not found. Check if default branch is not 'main'" | | 404 | Token, with path | "Path '{path}' not found or insufficient permissions." | | 403/429 | No token | Raise exception: "Rate limit exceeded. Provide a token." | | 403/429 | With token | Sleep using X-RateLimit-Reset header, recursive retry |

No LLM call. Routes to "direct" or "batch". Writes shared["max_tokens"], shared["file_batches"], shared["directory_tree"].

ContextRouter Algorithm: 1. Auto-detect max_tokens from provider if not set; write to shared["max_tokens"] 2. Measure prompt overhead = max(template_tokens for tutorial/advanced map_abstractions.md) + directory_tree_tokens 3. safety_limit = int(max_tokens * 0.95); effective_limit = safety_limit - prompt_overhead 4. Count total file content tokens using f"--- File Index {i}: {path} ---\n{content}\n\n" per file 5. If total_tokens > effective_limit OR force_batch: - Group files by os.path.dirname(path) — NEVER mix directories - Within each directory group, create batches respecting both effective_limit tokens AND batch_size file count - Return "batch" 6. Else: Return "direct"

dirname/
  filename.ext (idx:0)
  other.ext (idx:1)
other_dir/
  file.ext (idx:2)

\033[93m  [Debug] Batch {idx}: {len(batch)} files, ~{content_tokens:,} content tokens (limit: {effective_limit:,})\033[0m
\033[92m    - [{i}] {path}\033[0m

from pocketflow import Flow
from nodes import (
    FetchRepo, ContextRouter, MapAbstractions, ReduceAbstractions,
    IdentifyAbstractions, AnalyzeRelationships, OrderChapters,
    WriteChapters, CombineTutorial, DeterministicFileMapper
)

def create_tutorial_flow():
    fetch_repo = FetchRepo()
    context_router = ContextRouter()
    map_abstractions = MapAbstractions(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    reduce_abstractions = ReduceAbstractions(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    identify_abstractions = IdentifyAbstractions(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    analyze_relationships = AnalyzeRelationships(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    order_chapters = OrderChapters(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    write_chapters = WriteChapters(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    combine_tutorial = CombineTutorial()
    deterministic_mapper = DeterministicFileMapper(max_retries=5, wait=20)

    fetch_repo >> context_router

    context_router - "direct" >> identify_abstractions
    context_router - "batch" >> map_abstractions
    context_router - "deterministic" >> deterministic_mapper

    map_abstractions >> reduce_abstractions

    identify_abstractions >> analyze_relationships
    reduce_abstractions >> analyze_relationships

    analyze_relationships >> order_chapters
    order_chapters >> write_chapters

    deterministic_mapper >> write_chapters

    return Flow(start=fetch_repo)

def create_token_counter():

    try:

        return lambda text: len(enc.encode(text, disallowed_special=()))

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The flow.py module defines the core execution graph and orchestration logic for the Codebase-Knowledge-Builder system. Built on top of the pocketflow framework, this module is responsible for instantiating the individual pipeline nodes, configuring their operational retry and backoff parameters, and defining the conditional and linear execution edges that govern repository processing and tutorial generation.

The flow models three distinct processing strategies based on repository context size and structure: 1. Direct Path (direct): Bypasses abstraction chunking for smaller codebases by feeding repository context directly into abstraction identification. 2. Batch Path (batch): Employs map-reduce abstraction extraction for large codebases requiring parallel or batched decomposition. 3. Deterministic Path (deterministic): Uses a direct deterministic file mapping pipeline that maps repository source files to tutorial chapters, bypassing relationship analysis and chapter ordering.

All paths ultimately converge to produce chapter content and combine them into a unified tutorial artifact.

    write_chapters = WriteChapters(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    combine_tutorial = CombineTutorial()
    deterministic_mapper = DeterministicFileMapper(max_retries=5, wait=20)

    fetch_repo >> context_router

    context_router - "direct" >> identify_abstractions
    context_router - "batch" >> map_abstractions
    context_router - "deterministic" >> deterministic_mapper

    map_abstractions >> reduce_abstractions

    identify_abstractions >> analyze_relationships
    reduce_abstractions >> analyze_relationships

    analyze_relationships >> order_chapters
    order_chapters >> write_chapters

    deterministic_mapper >> write_chapters

    write_chapters >> combine_tutorial

    return Flow(start=fetch_repo)

The construction sequence instantiates eight processing nodes and one routing node. Nodes performing external language model calls (MapAbstractions, ReduceAbstractions, IdentifyAbstractions, AnalyzeRelationships, OrderChapters, WriteChapters, and DeterministicFileMapper) are initialized with max_retries=5 and wait=20 to ensure stability against model provider rate limits and transient connection dropouts. In contrast, purely deterministic data preparation nodes (FetchRepo, ContextRouter, and CombineTutorial) are initialized with default parameters as they do not perform remote API calls.

Routing rules established via the - "action" >> syntax map the string outcomes emitted by ContextRouter.prep() to downstream execution paths: - When context_router outputs "direct", execution proceeds immediately to identify_abstractions, bypassing intermediate abstraction mapping. - When context_router outputs "batch", execution is routed to map_abstractions, which iterates over chunked repository contents before passing intermediate representations to reduce_abstractions. - When context_router outputs "deterministic", execution branches to deterministic_mapper, which assigns chapters directly to files and connects directly into write_chapters, bypassing analyze_relationships and order_chapters.

Both the identify_abstractions and reduce_abstractions nodes feed into analyze_relationships, joining the direct and batched pathways. Downstream from chapter ordering, the write_chapters node receives dependencies from either order_chapters or deterministic_mapper. Finally, all generated chapter files are compiled into a unified tutorial via combine_tutorial. The function returns a Flow instance with start=fetch_repo.

docs.title: main()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def main() -> None:

Description: Initializes CLI parsing via argparse.ArgumentParser, processes source target arguments (GitHub URL or local filesystem directory), resolves token authentication, applies operational documentation modes (tutorial, advanced, api-reference, sdk), manages incremental manifest state, compiles the shared dictionary, executes the flow engine via create_tutorial_flow, and optionally cleans runtime artifacts.

Parameters: * None (reads from sys.argv and system environment variables).

Returns: * None

Raises: * SystemExit: Raised implicitly by argparse.ArgumentParser.parse_args() when invalid or missing required CLI arguments are encountered (e.g., neither --repo nor --dir specified). * Exception: Catches and logs generic file system exceptions during log/cache removal if --cleanup is enabled.

Implementation Logic:

def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Generate a tutorial for a GitHub codebase or local directory.")

    # Create mutually exclusive group for source
    source_group = parser.add_mutually_exclusive_group(required=True)
    source_group.add_argument("--repo", help="URL of the public GitHub repository.")
    source_group.add_argument("--dir", help="Path to local directory.")

    parser.add_argument("-n", "--name", help="Project name (optional, derived from repo/directory if omitted).")
    parser.add_argument("-t", "--token", help="GitHub personal access token (optional, reads from GITHUB_TOKEN env var if not provided).")
    parser.add_argument("-o", "--output", default="output", help="Base directory for output (default: ./output).")
    parser.add_argument("-i", "--include", nargs="+", help="Files to include (e.g., '*.py' '*.js'). Defaults to '*' (all files).")
    parser.add_argument(
        "-e",
        "--exclude",
        nargs="+",
        help="Files to exclude. Custom patterns are automatically merged with a massive global exclusion list (build caches, node_modules, binaries, media, AI environments) AND your repository's native .gitignore rules.",
    )
    parser.add_argument("-s", "--max-size", type=int, default=200000, help="Maximum file size in bytes (default: 200000, about 200KB).")
    # Add language parameter for multi-language support
    parser.add_argument("--language", default="english", help="Language for the generated tutorial (default: english)")
    # Add use_cache parameter to control LLM caching
    parser.add_argument("--no-cache", action="store_true", help="Disable LLM response caching (default: caching enabled)")
    # Add cleanup parameter
    parser.add_argument("--cleanup", action="store_true", help="Clean up logs and cache JSON at the end of the script (default: No)")
    # Add max_abstraction_num parameter to control the number of abstractions
    parser.add_argument("--max-abstractions", type=int, default=10, help="Maximum number of abstractions to identify (default: 10)")
    # Add thinking_level parameter for LLM reasoning capabilities
    parser.add_argument(
        "--thinking-level", default=None, help="Thinking effort level for OpenRouter models (e.g., low, medium, high). Default is auto."
    )
    # Add max_tokens parameter
    parser.add_argument(
        "--max-tokens", type=int, default=None, help="Maximum number of tokens for the context window (default: fetched dynamically)."
    )

    # --- Documentation Mode & Generation Styles ---
    parser.add_argument(
        "--mode",
        choices=["tutorial", "advanced", "api-reference", "sdk"],
        default="tutorial",
        help="Documentation style (tutorial, advanced, api-reference, sdk). (default: tutorial)",
    )
    parser.add_argument("--advanced", action="store_true", help="Legacy flag: equivalent to --mode advanced")
    parser.add_argument("--mkdocs", action="store_true", help="Format output for MkDocs Material (adds YAML frontmatter & nav snippet)")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--incremental", action="store_true", help="Enable MD5 incremental caching to skip unchanged modules (Only supported in --mode api-reference)"
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--force-rebuild", action="store_true", help="Clear incremental cache and regenerate all chapters from scratch (use with --incremental)"
    )

    # Add batching parameters
    parser.add_argument("--batch", type=int, default=50, help="Max files per batch in map-reduce mode")
    parser.add_argument("--force-batch", action="store_true", help="Force map-reduce mode regardless of context size")
    # Debug mode
    parser.add_argument("--debug", action="store_true", help="Enable verbose debug output")

    args = parser.parse_args()
    # ... [Token, mode resolution, force-rebuild manifest cleanup, shared dict initialization] ...

The argument parser establishes a mutually exclusive group requiring either --repo or --dir. It then provides flags for target naming, directory overrides, inclusion and exclusion pattern lists, context constraints, thinking level overrides, output styling modes (tutorial, advanced, api-reference, sdk), MkDocs integration flags, and batching constraints.

    # Resolve mode (backward compatibility for --advanced)
    doc_mode = "advanced" if args.advanced else args.mode

    # Enforce incremental cache constraints
    if args.incremental and doc_mode != "api-reference":
        print(
            "\n\033[93m[Warning] --incremental caching is only effective in 'api-reference' mode due to stable 1:1 file mapping. Disabling incremental cache for this run.\033[0m\n"
        )
        args.incremental = False

    # Handle --force-rebuild: delete the cache manifest to force fresh generation
    if args.force_rebuild and args.incremental:
        project_name = args.name
        if not project_name:
            # Derive project name the same way FetchRepo does
            if args.dir:
                project_name = os.path.basename(os.path.abspath(args.dir))
            elif args.repo:
                project_name = args.repo.rstrip("/").split("/")[-1]
        if project_name:
            output_base = args.output or "output"
            manifest_path = os.path.join(output_base, project_name, ".doc_cache_manifest.json")
            if os.path.exists(manifest_path):
                os.remove(manifest_path)
                print(f"\033[93m[Force Rebuild] Deleted cache manifest: {manifest_path}\033[0m")
            else:
                print(f"\033[93m[Force Rebuild] No cache manifest found at {manifest_path} — all chapters will be generated fresh.\033[0m")
    elif args.force_rebuild and not args.incremental:
        print("\033[93m[Warning] --force-rebuild has no effect without --incremental. Ignoring.\033[0m")

The mode resolution handles legacy --advanced invocations by mapping them directly to doc_mode = "advanced". It checks the validity of --incremental mode; if requested outside of api-reference mode, a warning is emitted and incremental caching is deactivated because non-reference modes do not maintain stable 1:1 module mappings. When --force-rebuild is supplied along with --incremental, the manifest path (.doc_cache_manifest.json) within the derived target directory is identified and removed prior to pipeline execution.

    # Prepare shared store to be passed between nodes
    shared = {
        "repo_url": args.repo,
        "local_dir": args.dir,
        "project_name": args.name,  # Can be None, FetchRepo will derive it
        "github_token": github_token,
        "output_dir": args.output,  # Base directory for CombineTutorial output
        # Add include/exclude patterns and max file size
        "include_patterns": set(args.include) if args.include else DEFAULT_INCLUDE_PATTERNS,
        "exclude_patterns": DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS.union(set(args.exclude)) if args.exclude else DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS,
        "max_file_size": args.max_size,
        # Add language for multi-language support
        "language": args.language,
        # Add use_cache flag (inverse of no-cache flag)
        "use_cache": not args.no_cache,
        # Add max_abstraction_num parameter
        "max_abstraction_num": args.max_abstractions,
        # Add thinking_level for LLM reasoning capabilities
        "thinking_level": args.thinking_level,
        # Add max tokens override
        "max_tokens": args.max_tokens,
        # Added mode, mkdocs, and incremental
        "mode": doc_mode,
        "mkdocs": args.mkdocs,
        "incremental": args.incremental,
        "advanced_mode": doc_mode == "advanced",
        # Batching settings
        "batch_size": args.batch,
        "force_batch": args.force_batch,
        # Debug mode
        "debug": args.debug,
        # Outputs will be populated by the nodes
        "files": [],
        "abstractions": [],
        "relationships": {},
        "chapter_order": [],
        "chapters": [],
        "final_output_dir": None,
    }

The blackboard shared dictionary is initialized with configuration parameters, pattern filters, output formats, token limits, and empty output collections (files, abstractions, relationships, chapter_order, chapters). This mutable dictionary is passed across all sequential and conditional nodes in the execution graph.

    # Configure per-run logging: logs/{project}_{mode}_{datetime}.log
    log_file = configure_logging(project_name=log_project_name, mode=doc_mode)

    # Display configuration
    # ... [Configuration printouts to stdout] ...

    # Create the flow instance
    tutorial_flow = create_tutorial_flow()

    # Run the flow
    tutorial_flow.run(shared)

    # Cleanup logs and cache if requested
    if args.cleanup:
        print("\nCleaning up cache and logs...")
        cache_path = "llm_cache.json"
        if os.path.exists(cache_path):
            try:
                os.remove(cache_path)
                print(f" - Removed {cache_path}")
            except Exception as e:
                print(f" - Failed to remove {cache_path}: {e}")

        log_dir = os.environ.get("LOG_DIR", "logs")
        if os.path.exists(log_dir) and os.path.isdir(log_dir):
            import shutil

            try:
                shutil.rmtree(log_dir)
                print(f" - Removed {log_dir} directory")
            except Exception as e:
                print(f" - Failed to remove {log_dir}: {e}")

The execution phase derives the active LLM provider (LLM_PROVIDER or fallback GEMINI), calculates context lengths via get_model_context_length(), sets up run-specific file logging via configure_logging(), and calls tutorial_flow.run(shared). If the --cleanup flag was set, it removes llm_cache.json and the logs directory using os.remove and shutil.rmtree.

Example: 

# Entry point invocation from source
if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The nodes.py module defines the discrete execution units (nodes) comprising the documentation generation pipelines in Codebase-Knowledge-Builder. Built on top of the PocketFlow framework (Node and BatchNode base classes), each node implements a strict three-phase lifecycle: 1. prep(shared): Extracts, transforms, and validates necessary data from the pipeline's shared dictionary state, pre-allocating token budgets or structuring batch payloads. 2. exec(prep_res): Executes core computational logic or orchestrates LLM interactions (via utils.call_llm) without mutating shared state directly. 3. post(shared, prep_res, exec_res): Writes computed results back to the shared dictionary and returns routing actions to control downstream graph transitions.

The module supports multiple documentation operational modes (tutorial, advanced, sdk, and api-reference), handling dynamic context routing, token estimation, Map-Reduce abstractions for large repositories, LLM-based architectural relationship extraction, chapter sequencing, incremental caching, and Markdown/MkDocs documentation generation.

docs.title: get_content_for_indices()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def get_content_for_indices(files_data: list, indices: list) -> dict:

Description: Resolves raw file contents from a list of indexed file tuples (path, content) given a list of integer indices. It constructs a dictionary keyed by formatted index comments ("{i} # {path}"), allowing downstream LLM prompts to reference code files with clear provenance.

Parameters: * files_data (list): List of tuples containing (file_path, file_content). * indices (list): List of integer indices to extract.

Returns: * dict: Mapping of string keys ("{index} # {path}") to file content strings.

Raises: None. Bounds checking is applied internally (0 <= i < len(files_data)).

Example: 

def get_content_for_indices(files_data, indices):
    content_map = {}
    for i in indices:
        if 0 <= i < len(files_data):
            path, content = files_data[i]
            content_map[f"{i} # {path}"] = content  # Use index + path as key for context
    return content_map

This helper function acts as an index-to-content resolver for nodes that map abstract architectural components to their underlying source files (such as WriteChapters). By formatting dictionary keys with # {path}, it embeds human-readable path identifiers into context blocks passed to LLMs while preserving zero-based index mapping. Any out-of-bounds index requests are safely skipped, avoiding index errors when mapping partial or filtered codebases.

docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def load_prompt_template(template_name: str, advanced_mode: bool = False, mode: str = None) -> str:

Description: Loads the raw Markdown prompt template file from the prompts/ directory tree based on the active operational mode (tutorial, advanced, sdk, or api-reference).

Parameters: * template_name (str): Base name of the prompt Markdown file (without .md). * advanced_mode (bool, optional): Legacy flag determining if advanced or tutorial folder is used when mode is None. Defaults to False. * mode (str, optional): Specific mode folder name under prompts/. Defaults to None.

Returns: * str: Raw template content string loaded with UTF-8-SIG encoding.

Raises: * FileNotFoundError: If the constructed template path does not exist on disk.

Example: 

def load_prompt_template(template_name, advanced_mode=False, mode=None):
    """Load a prompt template file from the prompts/ directory."""
    if mode is None:
        prompt_dir = "advanced" if advanced_mode else "tutorial"
    else:
        prompt_dir = mode

    path = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "prompts", prompt_dir, f"{template_name}.md")
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
        return f.read()

This function resolves dynamic prompt templates from the file system relative to nodes.py. When mode is explicitly provided, it directly selects the subdirectory corresponding to that mode; otherwise, it falls back to checking the boolean advanced_mode parameter. Files are loaded with utf-8-sig encoding to handle potential byte-order marks transparently.

docs.title: parse_yaml_response()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def parse_yaml_response(response: str) -> any:

Description: Extracts and safely parses structured YAML text blocks enclosed within standard Markdown triple backtick blocks (```yaml) from an LLM response string.

Parameters: * response (str): Raw string returned by the LLM call.

Returns: * any: Parsed YAML data structures (typically list or dict).

Raises: * ValueError: If the string does not contain a ```yaml fenced block or if yaml.safe_load fails to parse the extracted content.

Example: 

def parse_yaml_response(response):
    """Extract and parse YAML from an LLM response fenced in ```yaml blocks."""
    try:
        yaml_str = response.strip().split("```yaml")[1].split("```")[0].strip()
        return yaml.safe_load(yaml_str)
    except Exception as e:
        raise ValueError(f"Failed to parse YAML: {e}") from e

LLM prompts in this framework mandate structured responses within fenced ```yaml blocks. This helper isolates the substring between the opening ```yaml tag and the closing ``` delimiter, applying yaml.safe_load. If the LLM generates malformed YAML, omit delimiters, or encounters syntax errors, the function wraps the underlying parser exception inside a descriptive ValueError to trigger upstream node retry mechanisms.

docs.title: create_token_counter()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def create_token_counter() -> callable:

Description: Instantiates and returns a token counter callable using OpenAI's tiktoken library with the cl100k_base encoding, falling back to a character heuristic (len(text) // 4) if tiktoken fails.

Parameters: None.

Returns: * callable: A function (str) -> int that accepts text and returns estimated token count.

Raises: None.

Example: 

def create_token_counter():
    """Create a token counting function using tiktoken with char-count fallback."""
    try:
        enc = tiktoken.get_encoding("cl100k_base")
        return lambda text: len(enc.encode(text, disallowed_special=()))
    except Exception:
        return lambda text: len(text) // 4

This factory creates a fast token estimator for pre-flight context budgeting across nodes. By passing disallowed_special=() to tiktoken.encode, the tokenizer safely encodes special tokens (such as <|endoftext|>) appearing inside raw source code files as ordinary text tokens. If encoding fails due to missing environment bindings or encoding errors, the closure degrades gracefully to the standard 4-characters-per-token heuristic.

docs.title: resolve_max_tokens()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def resolve_max_tokens(shared: dict) -> int:

Description: Determines the maximum context token window for the configured LLM provider and model. Checks shared["max_tokens"] first, and if not present, inspects environment variables and queries provider metadata via utils.call_llm.get_model_context_length.

Parameters: * shared (dict): The pipeline shared state dictionary.

Returns: * int: The maximum allowed context length in tokens.

Raises: None.

Example: 

def resolve_max_tokens(shared):
    """Resolve max_tokens from shared store or auto-detect from provider env vars."""
    max_tokens = shared.get("max_tokens")
    if max_tokens is not None:
        return max_tokens
    provider = os.environ.get("LLM_PROVIDER")
    if provider == "GEMINI" or not provider:
        endpoint = "https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com"
        model_name = os.getenv("GEMINI_MODEL", "gemini-3.7-flash")
        api_key = os.getenv("GEMINI_API_KEY", "")
    else:
        endpoint = os.environ.get(f"{provider}_BASE_URL", "")
        model_name = os.environ.get(f"{provider}_MODEL", "")
        api_key = os.environ.get(f"{provider}_API_KEY", "")
    return get_model_context_length(endpoint, model_name, api_key)

This function centrally resolves model context capacities across different LLM backends. If an explicit limit is present in the pipeline's shared configuration, it takes precedence. Otherwise, it detects whether Gemini or an alternative OpenAI-compatible provider (such as Anthropic, DeepSeek, or a local endpoint) is active, extracts connection environment variables, and queries get_model_context_length() to obtain the upper bound for prompt budgeting.

docs.text: Inherits from: pocketflow.Node Description: Node used in api-reference mode to bypass high-level abstraction discovery and instead map every valid source code file into a 1:1 chapter/module reference page. It uses an LLM to filter out non-code assets (such as lockfiles or configs).

docs.title: DeterministicFileMapper.prep()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def prep(self, shared: dict) -> tuple:

Description: Formats all ingested files into an indexed listing and constructs a filtering prompt via utils.prompts.build_code_file_filter_prompt.

Parameters: * shared (dict): Pipeline shared store containing files and project_name.

Returns: * tuple: (prompt: str, thinking_level: any, max_tokens: int).

Example: 

    def prep(self, shared):
        files_data = shared["files"]
        project_name = shared["project_name"]

        file_listing = "\n".join([f"{i} # {path}" for i, (path, _) in enumerate(files_data)])

        prompt = build_code_file_filter_prompt(project_name, file_listing)
        return prompt, shared.get("thinking_level", None), shared.get("max_tokens", 100000)

The prep method extracts the list of (path, content) tuples from shared["files"] and creates an enumerated string where each entry contains the file index and file path. It formats these into the code filter prompt using build_code_file_filter_prompt, passing the prompt, configured thinking level, and maximum tokens to the execution stage.

docs.title: DeterministicFileMapper.exec()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def exec(self, prep_res: tuple) -> list:

Description: Dispatches the filtering prompt to the LLM and parses the YAML response containing the list of integer indices corresponding to actual code files.

Parameters: * prep_res (tuple): (prompt, thinking_level, max_tokens).

Returns: * list: List of valid integer file indices (List[int]).

Raises: * Exception: Propagates any LLM execution or parsing failure to trigger PocketFlow node retries.

Example: 

    def exec(self, prep_res):
        try:
            prompt, thinking_level, max_tokens = prep_res
            log_token_estimation(self.__class__.__name__, prompt, max_tokens)
            print("Smartly filtering non-code files using LLM...")
            response = call_llm(prompt, use_cache=True, thinking_level=thinking_level)
            valid_indices = parse_yaml_response(response)
            if not isinstance(valid_indices, list):
                valid_indices = []
            return [int(idx) for idx in valid_indices]
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"\033[93m[Node {self.__class__.__name__} Retry Triggered] Error: {e}\033[0m")
            llm_logger.error(f"[Node {self.__class__.__name__}] Error: {e}", exc_info=True)
            raise e

exec records token estimation telemetry via utils.token_utils.log_token_estimation before calling utils.call_llm.call_llm with caching enabled. The returned YAML string is parsed into a list of indices. If an error occurs, the exception is logged to llm_logger and re-raised to allow PocketFlow's retry mechanism to handle intermittent network or formatting errors.

docs.title: DeterministicFileMapper.post()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def post(self, shared: dict, prep_res: tuple, exec_res: list) -> str:

Description: Iterates over all files, skips non-code files, creates 1:1 abstraction records for each valid file, and populates shared["abstractions"], shared["chapter_order"], and shared["relationships"].

Parameters: * shared (dict): Pipeline shared state. * prep_res (tuple): Execution preparation artifacts. * exec_res (list): List of valid file indices.

Returns: * str: "default" routing action.

Example: 

    def post(self, shared, prep_res, exec_res):
        import os

        files = shared.get("files", [])
        valid_indices = set(exec_res)
        modules = []
        chapter_order = []

        for idx, (file_path, _content) in enumerate(files):
            if idx not in valid_indices:
                print(f"  - Skipping non-code file: {file_path}")
                continue

            clean_name = os.path.splitext(file_path)[0].replace(os.sep, ".").replace("/", ".")

            modules.append(
                {"name": clean_name, "description": f"Internal API reference for `{file_path}`", "files": [idx], "original_path": file_path}
            )
            chapter_order.append(len(modules) - 1)

        shared["abstractions"] = modules
        shared["chapter_order"] = chapter_order
        shared["relationships"] = {"summary": "Deterministic Internal API Reference.", "details": []}
        print(f"\033[92m[DeterministicFileMapper] Mapped {len(modules)} ACTUAL code files for exhaustive documentation.\033[0m")
        return "default"

The post step converts each retained code file into a dot-separated module identifier (e.g., utils/call_llm.py becomes utils.call_llm). It constructs a 1:1 mapping entry with original path tracking and sets up sequential chapter ordering. It also initializes an empty relationship dictionary, ensuring all downstream nodes receive consistent data structures.

docs.title: Class ContextRouter
docs.text: Inherits from: pocketflow.Node Description: Inspects total repository file size and token overhead against the model's effective context limit. Routes execution to "deterministic" (for api-reference mode), "direct" (single-prompt abstraction discovery), or "batch" (directory-preserving Map-Reduce chunking).

docs.title: ContextRouter.prep()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def prep(self, shared: dict) -> tuple:

Description: Computes prompt overhead (template tokens, directory tree tokens, listing tokens) and file content tokens. Calculates effective token limit (95% of max_tokens - overhead) and determines the appropriate route.

Parameters: * shared (dict): Pipeline shared store.

Returns: * tuple: Route tuple containing (route, files_data, effective_limit, batch_size, file_token_map, count_tokens, directory_tree, debug).

Example: 

    def prep(self, shared):
        files_data = shared["files"]
        max_tokens = resolve_max_tokens(shared)

        shared["max_tokens"] = max_tokens

        # --- Token estimation setup ---
        count_tokens = create_token_counter()

        # --- Calculate prompt overhead FIRST ---
        // ... prompt overhead calculation: template, directory tree, file listing ...
        prompt_overhead = max_template_tokens + tree_tokens + listing_tokens

        # --- Effective limit = safety margin minus overhead ---
        safety_limit = int(max_tokens * 0.95)
        effective_limit = safety_limit - prompt_overhead
        force_batch = shared.get("force_batch", False)

        if shared.get("mode", "tutorial") == "api-reference":
            return ("deterministic", files_data, effective_limit, shared.get("batch_size", 50), None, None, directory_tree, False)

        if total_tokens > effective_limit or force_batch:
            return (
                "batch", files_data, effective_limit, shared.get("batch_size", 50),
                file_token_map, count_tokens, directory_tree, shared.get("debug", False),
            )
        else:
            return ("direct", files_data, effective_limit, shared.get("batch_size", 50), None, None, directory_tree, False)

prep computes the prompt overhead by measuring the template size across tutorial and advanced folders, generating a directory tree, and indexing all files. A 5% safety margin is deducted from max_tokens before subtracting overhead to establish the effective_limit. If the total tokens exceed this limit or force_batch is active, the node selects the "batch" route; if the mode is api-reference, it returns "deterministic"; otherwise, it returns "direct".

docs.title: ContextRouter.exec()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def exec(self, prep_res: tuple) -> Union[str, list]:

Description: If routed to "batch", groups files by directory and splits them into token-aware and count-aware chunks without mixing directories across batches.

Parameters: * prep_res (tuple): Output tuple from prep.

Returns: * Union[str, list]: "direct", "deterministic", or a list of batches List[List[Tuple[int, str, str]]].

Example: 

    def exec(self, prep_res):
        route, files_data, effective_limit, batch_size, file_token_map, _count_tokens, directory_tree, debug = prep_res
        llm_logger.info(
            f"NODE EXEC | node=ContextRouter | action=route_decision | route={route} | files={len(files_data)} | effective_limit={effective_limit:,}"
        )

        if route == "direct":
            return "direct"
        if route == "deterministic":
            return "deterministic"

        dir_groups = defaultdict(list)
        for i, (path, content) in enumerate(files_data):
            dir_groups[os.path.dirname(path)].append((i, path, content, file_token_map[i]))

        batches = []
        for dirname in sorted(dir_groups.keys()):
            current_batch = []
            current_tokens = 0

            for i, path, content, tokens in dir_groups[dirname]:
                if current_batch and (current_tokens + tokens > effective_limit or len(current_batch) >= batch_size):
                    batches.append(current_batch)
                    current_batch = []
                    current_tokens = 0

                current_batch.append((i, path, content))
                current_tokens += tokens

            if current_batch:
                batches.append(current_batch)

        self._directory_tree = directory_tree
        return batches

For "direct" and "deterministic" routes, exec acts as a pass-through. For batching, it organizes files by directory using defaultdict(list). It iterates through each directory's files, packing them into batches that strictly respect both effective_limit token budgets and batch_size item ceilings. Batches never mix files from different parent directories, preserving local architectural coherence.

docs.title: ContextRouter.post()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def post(self, shared: dict, prep_res: tuple, exec_res: Union[str, list]) -> str:

Description: Writes the generated file batches and directory tree into shared memory and returns the routing branch key.

Parameters: * shared (dict): Shared state dictionary. * prep_res (tuple): Data returned from prep. * exec_res (Union[str, list]): Result from exec.

Returns: * str: Route string ("direct", "deterministic", or "batch").

Example: 

    def post(self, shared, prep_res, exec_res):
        if exec_res == "direct":
            return "direct"
        if exec_res == "deterministic":
            return "deterministic"
        shared["file_batches"] = exec_res
        # Reuse directory tree built during prep()
        shared["directory_tree"] = getattr(self, "_directory_tree", self._build_directory_tree(shared["files"]))
        return "batch"

The post method assigns execution results according to the chosen route. When running in "batch" mode, it saves file_batches and the generated directory_tree into the shared state dictionary and returns "batch" to instruct PocketFlow to trigger the MapAbstractions batch node.

docs.title: ContextRouter._build_directory_tree()
docs.text:
Visibility: Protected (Static) Signature: def _build_directory_tree(files_data: list) -> str:

Description: Generates a compact plaintext tree representation of the codebase hierarchy, noting file indices alongside filenames.

Parameters: * files_data (list): List of (path, content) tuples.

Returns: * str: Formatted directory tree string.

Example: 

    @staticmethod
    def _build_directory_tree(files_data):
        """Build a compact directory tree string from the list of (path, content) tuples."""
        from collections import defaultdict

        dir_files = defaultdict(list)
        for i, (path, _content) in enumerate(files_data):
            dirname = os.path.dirname(path) or "."
            basename = os.path.basename(path)
            dir_files[dirname].append(f"{basename} (idx:{i})")

        lines = []
        for dirname in sorted(dir_files.keys()):
            lines.append(f"{dirname}/")
            lines.extend(f"  {fname}" for fname in sorted(dir_files[dirname]))
        return "\n".join(lines)

This static method aggregates all repository file paths by their directory names. It sorts directories and files alphabetically, appending the integer index (idx:{i}) to each file entry. This provides the LLM with a concise structural map of the entire project repository within minimal token overhead.

docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def exec(self, item: dict) -> list:

Description: Formats batch file contents and directory context into the map_abstractions prompt, calls the LLM, and parses/validates the returned YAML abstraction entries.

Parameters: * item (dict): Batch item parameters from prep().

Returns: * list: List of validated abstraction dictionaries ([{"name": str, "description": str, "files": List[int]}]).

Example: 

    def exec(self, item):
        batch_index = item["batch_index"]
        files = item["files"]
        print(f"Mapping abstractions for batch {batch_index} ({len(files)} files)...")

        context = ""
        file_listing_for_prompt = []
        for i, path, content in files:
            context += f"--- File Index {i}: {path} ---\n{content}\n\n"
            file_listing_for_prompt.append(f"- {i} # {path}")

        file_listing = "\n".join(file_listing_for_prompt)
        prompt_template = load_prompt_template("map_abstractions", mode=item.get("mode", "tutorial"))

        // ... language hints and prompt formatting ...
        response = call_llm(prompt, use_cache=(item["use_cache"] and self.cur_retry == 0), thinking_level=item["thinking_level"])
        abstractions = parse_yaml_response(response)

        validated_abstractions = []
        if isinstance(abstractions, list):
            for obj in abstractions:
                if isinstance(obj, dict) and "name" in obj and "description" in obj and "file_indices" in obj:
                    import re
                    validated_indices = []
                    for idx_entry in obj["file_indices"]:
                        nums = re.findall(r"\d+", str(idx_entry))
                        if nums:
                            validated_indices.append(int(nums[0]))
                    if validated_indices:
                        validated_abstractions.append(
                            {"name": obj["name"], "description": obj["description"], "files": sorted(set(validated_indices))}
                        )
        return validated_abstractions

exec formats the batch's code files and file listing into the prompt template. After invoking call_llm and parse_yaml_response, it validates that each returned abstraction contains name, description, and file_indices. Regex extraction normalizes file indices into integer lists, ensuring resilient parsing even if the LLM includes markdown annotations or comments in the index entries.

docs.title: Class IdentifyAbstractions
docs.text: Inherits from: pocketflow.Node Description: Single-prompt abstraction extraction node executed when the codebase fits within the active context window ("direct" route).

docs.title: IdentifyAbstractions.prep()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def prep(self, shared: dict) -> tuple:

Description: Constructs a single token-budgeted context string containing all files, truncating if necessary to stay within the 95% model context safety limit.

Parameters: * shared (dict): Pipeline shared store.

Returns: * tuple: Context string, file listing, total file count, and prompt configuration arguments.

Example: 

    def prep(self, shared):
        files_data = shared["files"]
        project_name = shared["project_name"]
        language = shared.get("language", "english")
        use_cache = shared.get("use_cache", True)
        max_abstraction_num = shared.get("max_abstraction_num", 10)
        thinking_level = shared.get("thinking_level", None)

        def create_llm_context(files_data):
            max_tokens = resolve_max_tokens(shared)
            safety_limit = int(max_tokens * 0.95)
            count_tokens = create_token_counter()
            context = ""
            file_info = []
            current_tokens = 0

            for i, (path, content) in enumerate(files_data):
                entry = f"--- File Index {i}: {path} ---\n{content}\n\n"
                entry_tokens = count_tokens(entry)
                if current_tokens + entry_tokens > safety_limit:
                    print(f"\033[93mWarning: Context truncated at file index {i} ({path}) to fit within limit of {safety_limit} tokens.\033[0m")
                    break
                context += entry
                file_info.append((i, path))
                current_tokens += entry_tokens

            return context, file_info

        context, file_info = create_llm_context(files_data)
        file_listing_for_prompt = "\n".join([f"- {idx} # {path}" for idx, path in file_info])
        return (
            context, file_listing_for_prompt, len(files_data), project_name,
            language, use_cache, max_abstraction_num, thinking_level,
            shared.get("advanced_mode", False), shared.get("max_tokens", 100000), shared.get("mode", "tutorial"),
        )

prep uses an internal helper create_llm_context to pack files into a formatted prompt buffer while monitoring token usage via create_token_counter(). If the cumulative tokens exceed 95% of max_tokens, it truncates the context and logs a warning. It returns the formatted context string alongside file listing metadata.

Returns: * list: List of validated abstraction dictionaries ([{"name": str, "description": str, "files": List[int]}]).

    def prep(self, shared):

        # Budget is split EVENLY across abstractions so later ones aren't starved.

        max_tokens = shared.get("max_tokens", 100000)
        safety_limit = int(max_tokens * 0.95)
        prompt_overhead = 2000
        estimate_tokens = create_token_counter()
        current_tokens = estimate_tokens(context)
        total_budget = safety_limit - current_tokens - prompt_overhead
        num_abstractions = len(abstractions)

        # Pre-compute file token sizes for all abstractions (sorted largest first)
        // ... size computation ...

        # Two-pass allocation:
        # Pass 1: give each abstraction an equal share, track unused
        # Pass 2: redistribute unused budget to abstractions that need more
        per_abstr_budget = total_budget // max(num_abstractions, 1)
        // ... pass 1 allocation and pass 2 rollover logic ...

        return (
            context, "\n".join(abstraction_info_for_prompt), num_abstractions,
            project_name, language, use_cache, thinking_level,
            shared.get("advanced_mode", False), shared.get("max_tokens", 100000), shared.get("mode", "tutorial"),

prep uses a two-pass budget distribution strategy to prevent prompt token starvation across abstractions. In Pass 1, each abstraction receives an equal share (total_budget // num_abstractions) to include its largest source files. docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def exec(self, prep_res: tuple) -> list:

Description: Calls the LLM with the order_chapters template and validates that the returned sequence is a valid permutation containing each abstraction index exactly once.

Parameters: * prep_res (tuple): Context and parameters from prep().

Returns: * list: Ordered list of abstraction indices (List[int]).

Raises: * ValueError: If the sequence contains duplicates, out-of-bounds indices, or missing items. * Exception: Re-raises errors for retry handling.

Example: 

    def exec(self, prep_res):
        try:
            (
                abstraction_listing, context, num_abstractions, project_name,
                list_lang_note, use_cache, thinking_level, _advanced_mode, max_tokens, doc_mode,
            ) = prep_res

            prompt_template = load_prompt_template("order_chapters", mode=doc_mode)
            prompt = prompt_template.format(
                project_name=project_name, list_lang_note=list_lang_note, abstraction_listing=abstraction_listing, context=context
            )
            log_token_estimation(self.__class__.__name__, prompt, max_tokens)
            response = call_llm(prompt, use_cache=(use_cache and self.cur_retry == 0), thinking_level=thinking_level)

            ordered_indices_raw = parse_yaml_response(response)
            if not isinstance(ordered_indices_raw, list):
                raise ValueError("LLM output is not a list")

            ordered_indices = []
            seen_indices = set()
            for entry in ordered_indices_raw:
                idx = int(str(entry).split("#")[0].strip())
                if not (0 <= idx < num_abstractions) or idx in seen_indices:
                    raise ValueError(f"Invalid or duplicate index {idx}")
                ordered_indices.append(idx)
                seen_indices.add(idx)

            if len(ordered_indices) != num_abstractions:
                raise ValueError(f"Ordered list length mismatch. Missing: {set(range(num_abstractions)) - seen_indices}")

            return ordered_indices
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"\033[93m[Node {self.__class__.__name__} Retry Triggered] Error: {e}\033[0m")
            llm_logger.error(f"[Node {self.__class__.__name__}] Error: {e}", exc_info=True)
            raise e

exec validates the chapter sequence returned by the LLM. It parses each entry to an integer, verifies that every index is within [0, num_abstractions - 1], checks for duplicates, and confirms that the length matches the total number of abstractions. If any validation step fails, it raises a ValueError to trigger an automatic retry.

    def exec(self, item):

            abstraction_name = item["abstraction_details"]["name"]
            chapter_num = item["chapter_num"]
            doc_mode = item.get("mode", "tutorial")
            incremental = item.get("incremental", False)

            file_context_str = "\n\n".join(
                f"--- File: {idx_path.split('# ')[1] if '# ' in idx_path else idx_path} ---\n{content}"
                for idx_path, content in item["related_files_content_map"].items()
            )

            # --- Incremental Caching Logic ---
            if incremental and output_dir:
                // ... MD5 hash check against .doc_cache_manifest.json ...
                # If cache hits, reads file, generates summary for context, and returns immediately

            previous_chapters_summary = "" if doc_mode == "api-reference" else "\n---\n".join(self.chapter_summaries)
            prompt_template = load_prompt_template("draft_chapters", mode=doc_mode)
            // ... format draft_chapters prompt ...
            chapter_content = call_llm(prompt, use_cache=(use_cache and self.cur_retry == 0), thinking_level=thinking_level)

            # Generate LLM summary for cross-chapter context (skip for api-reference)
            if doc_mode != "api-reference":
                summary_prompt = build_chapter_summary_prompt(chapter_num, abstraction_name, chapter_content, language)
                chapter_summary = call_llm(summary_prompt, use_cache=True, thinking_level=None)
                self.chapter_summaries.append(f"Chapter {chapter_num} — {abstraction_name.strip()}:\n{chapter_summary}")

            return {"content": chapter_content, "hash": current_hash, "name": abstraction_name}
        except Exception as e:

On a cache hit, it loads the existing chapter from disk and skips the drafting LLM call. 2. Context Summarization: Rather than appending entire previous chapters into the prompt (which would cause $O(n^2)$ token explosion), it generates a concise 3–5 sentence summary of each chapter via build_chapter_summary_prompt and appends it to self.chapter_summaries.

Visibility: Public Signature: def post(self, shared: dict, prep_res: list, exec_res_list: list) -> None:

Description: Saves all generated chapter contents to shared["chapters"], writes updated MD5 hashes to .doc_cache_manifest.json if incremental mode is active, and clears temporary instance state.

Parameters: * shared (dict): Pipeline shared store. * prep_res (list): List of prepared chapter items. * exec_res_list (list): List of result dictionaries from exec().

Returns: None.

Example: 

    def post(self, shared, prep_res, exec_res_list):
        import json
        import os

        shared["chapters"] = [res["content"] for res in exec_res_list]

        if shared.get("incremental"):
            output_dir = os.path.join(shared.get("output_dir", "output"), shared.get("project_name"))
            os.makedirs(output_dir, exist_ok=True)
            manifest_path = os.path.join(output_dir, ".doc_cache_manifest.json")

            manifest = {}
            if os.path.exists(manifest_path):
                try:
                    with open(manifest_path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
                        manifest = json.load(f)
                except Exception:
                    pass

            for res in exec_res_list:
                if res.get("hash") and res.get("name"):
                    manifest[res["name"]] = res["hash"]

            with open(manifest_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                json.dump(manifest, f, indent=2)

        del self.chapters_written_so_far
        del self.chapter_summaries
        print(f"Finished writing {len(exec_res_list)} chapters.")

If incremental mode is active, it merges the current run's content hashes into .doc_cache_manifest.json and writes the manifest to disk. Finally, it cleans up temporary instance variables (chapters_written_so_far and chapter_summaries) to free memory.

Following the graph execution mechanisms established in nodes, the utils package provides specialized lower-level helper components that support file ingestion, token accounting, prompt assembly, and large language model execution.

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
The utils/__init__.py file serves as the package initialization marker for the utils directory within the Codebase-Knowledge-Builder repository. In Python's package system, the presence of __init__.py marks the enclosing directory as a regular package rather than a namespace package, ensuring deterministic module resolution across diverse deployment environments and runtime configurations.

By remaining empty, this file establishes a zero-overhead package boundary. It intentionally avoids eager re-exports or top-level symbol imports from its sibling utility modules. This architectural design yields several benefits: 1. Prevents Circular Dependencies: Submodules like utils.call_llm and utils.prompts can import shared dependencies without triggering circular initialization chains through __init__.py. 2. Eliminates Initialization Overhead: Downstream modules that require a single utility (such as utils.token_utils) do not pay the runtime or memory penalty of importing heavy third-party networking or crawling libraries (e.g., requests, google-genai). 3. Encourages Explicit Module Namespaces: Consumers must import submodules explicitly (for example, from utils.call_llm import call_llm or from utils.crawl_local_files import crawl_local_files), ensuring clear call sites and straightforward static analysis.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The utils.call_llm module provides unified abstraction for interacting with Large Language Model (LLM) backends within the Codebase-Knowledge-Builder pipeline. It manages:

  • Dynamic Provider Routing: Dispatches requests to native Google Gemini SDK clients (google-genai targeting Gemini API or Google Cloud Vertex AI) or generic OpenAI-compatible HTTP endpoints (such as OpenRouter or local Ollama instances).
  • Caching Layer: Persists prompt-response pairs to a local JSON file cache (llm_cache.json) to minimize redundant latency and compute costs during iterative graph execution.
  • Reasoning and Thinking Level Control: Configures reasoning parameters across different providers, such as ThinkingConfig for Google Gemini and reasoning/think payloads for OpenRouter and Ollama.
  • Dynamic Context Discovery: Queries external model catalogs (e.g., OpenRouter API) to identify maximum context window constraints or applies safety defaults for Google Gemini.
  • Isolated Run-Level Logging: Sets up dedicated run logs under a designated directory (logs/) with sanitized filenames and formatted execution metadata.

docs.title: configure_logging()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def configure_logging(project_name="project", mode="tutorial") -> str:

Description: Initializes file-based logging for the active execution run. It creates the destination directory specified by the LOG_DIR environment variable (defaulting to "logs"), sanitizes the input project_name and mode strings against invalid filesystem characters, and generates a timestamped log file. It replaces all existing logger handlers with a configured logging.FileHandler encoded in UTF-8 and writes standard run header metadata.

Parameters: * project_name (str, optional): Identifier for the codebase/project being documented. Defaults to "project". * mode (str, optional): Processing mode identifier (e.g., "tutorial", "deep-dive"). Defaults to "tutorial".

Returns: * str: Absolute or relative file path to the newly created log file.

Raises: * OSError: If the directory creation fails or permissions prevent creating the log file.

Example: 

def configure_logging(project_name="project", mode="tutorial"):
    log_directory = os.getenv("LOG_DIR", "logs")
    os.makedirs(log_directory, exist_ok=True)

    # Sanitize project name for filesystem safety
    safe_project = "".join(c if c.isalnum() or c in "-_." else "_" for c in project_name)
    safe_mode = mode.replace("-", "_")
    timestamp = datetime.now().strftime("%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")
    log_file = os.path.join(log_directory, f"{safe_project}_{safe_mode}_{timestamp}.log")

    # Remove any existing handlers (e.g., NullHandler) and add the file handler
    logger.handlers.clear()
    file_handler = logging.FileHandler(log_file, encoding="utf-8")
    file_handler.setFormatter(logging.Formatter("%(asctime)s - %(levelname)s - %(message)s"))
    logger.addHandler(file_handler)

    # Log run metadata at the start of every log file
    logger.info(f"{'=' * 80}")
    logger.info(f"RUN STARTED | project={project_name} | mode={mode} | timestamp={timestamp}")
    logger.info(f"Log file: {log_file}")
    logger.info(f"{'=' * 80}")

    return log_file

configure_logging ensures file logging is deferred until command-line arguments are parsed in main. The sanitization step replaces non-alphanumeric and non-standard filename characters with underscores, preventing directory traversal or invalid path errors on diverse operating systems. Once instantiated, the handler isolates LLM logs from the root logger, capturing prompt transmissions, token estimates, and raw responses.

docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def load_cache() -> dict:

Description: Reads and deserializes the JSON cache stored at cache_file (llm_cache.json). If the file is missing, unreadable, or contains corrupted JSON data, the error is logged as a warning and an empty dictionary is returned.

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * dict: Key-value mapping representing cached prompts (str) to completions (str). Returns {} on failure.

Raises: * No exceptions are raised; errors are trapped internally and logged via logger.warning.

Example: 

def load_cache():
    try:
        with open(cache_file) as f:
            return json.load(f)
    except Exception:
        logger.warning("Failed to load cache.")
    return {}

The function provides fault-tolerant reading of cached prompts. It wraps standard file I/O within a blanket exception guard so that missing cache files or transient file lock errors do not disrupt the execution of downstream node generation tasks in nodes.

Description: Serializes and writes the provided dictionary to cache_file (llm_cache.json) in plaintext JSON format. Captures and logs any I/O errors encountered during the write operation.

Parameters: * cache (dict): The dictionary of prompt-to-response pairs to be saved to disk.

Returns: * None

Raises: * No exceptions are raised; errors are trapped internally and logged via logger.warning.

Example: 

def save_cache(cache):
    try:
        with open(cache_file, "w") as f:
            json.dump(cache, f)
    except Exception:
        logger.warning("Failed to save cache")

save_cache executes an atomic overwrite of the local cache file whenever an LLM invocation yields a new response. It acts synchronously within call_llm, allowing intermediate pipeline stages to preserve progress across intermittent network disconnects or process restarts.
